title.title: Strongly polynomial-time linear programming
title.subtitle: Claim: linear programs are solved in steps polynomial in the numbers of variables and constraints alone

plain: Linear programs plan the cheapest diet or schedule; claimed: the work never depends on how big the numbers are

beats.text: The simplex method walks along the edges of a polytope, corner to corner
A companion paper claims some walks must take superpolynomially many steps
So the new algorithm leaves the edges entirely; the picture is schematic

steps: Ask which of two subspaces holds a nonnegative witness
Rescale coordinates and trust only the largest signs
Fix coordinates one by one until linear algebra finishes

achievement.label: Smale's ninth problem
achievement.context: Before: polynomial in the bit length (Khachiyan, 1979), not in $m$ and $n$ alone
achievement.note: Lean covers rational data; real coefficients are manuscript only

verify.detail: Lean: the rational case and the Hirsch disproof; not real coefficients
verify.ourCheck: We read the Lean scope and the introductions; we did not referee

voice.text: Walking corner to corner can take forever, a companion paper claims. The new method never walks.
It looks at signs at many scales, then fixes coordinates one at a time.

sources.quote: Linear programs are solvable in time polynomial in their bit length (Khachiyan 1979)
simple rational polytopes with n facets and graph diameter n^{ω(1)} disprove the polynomial Hirsch conjecture
